answer: Randomness-gated voyage slots. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon assigns every registered agent a secret departure window; only agents whose window falls in the current ocean of time may submit work, and the assignment is revealed after commit. Because the beacon is unpredictable before the epoch, an attacker cannot precompute which sybil identities will be active, so flooding the registry yields mostly dormant slots. Each identity still pays registration plus per-epoch beacon-attendance proof, a recurring cost scaled to the nebula of idle identities they must maintain.
